news.title: The Block Reports Partial Binance Withdrawal Restoration After Estimated $6.3 Billion Theft
news.body: The Block reported that Binance suspended withdrawals after an October 30 theft estimated at $6.3 billion and subsequently restored access in stages. Its account distinguishes withdrawals already reopened from additional reopenings still planned; it does not establish restored access across every asset. The report also attributed to Elliptic a finding that attackers exchanged stolen tokens for $124 million in bitcoin. For payment providers and liquidity counterparties, asset-specific withdrawal availability and pending-transaction records remain necessary checks before moving funds or retrying transfers.

news.title: FinCEN and Fed Withdraw Proposed $250 Cross-Border Recordkeeping Threshold
news.body: Banks and remittance providers no longer need to prepare for this proposed expansion of federal transfer-record requirements. FinCEN and the Federal Reserve withdrew amendments that would have lowered the relevant cross-border Recordkeeping and Travel Rule threshold from $3,000 to $250 and expanded coverage of digital-asset transactions. The withdrawal removes those proposed changes, not existing anti-money-laundering, suspicious-activity reporting or Travel Rule obligations.

news.title: BILL Reports 12-Minute Underwriting Turnaround With Human Decisions Retained
news.body: BILL CEO René Lacerte said its three-agent Robin underwriting suite reduced case turnaround from three hours to approximately 12 minutes. Humans still make the credit decision. Lacerte also said more than 100 AI agents save BILL teams over 1,400 hours monthly. These management-reported figures describe faster processing, not independently verified cash savings or improved credit outcomes; approval quality, exception handling and subsequent losses remain separate measures for embedded-credit providers evaluating similar workflows.

news.title: Gnosis Pay Breach Exposes Customer Identity and Wallet Links
news.body: A Gnosis Pay customer notification listed exposure of a name, home address, card number and connected wallet addresses following unauthorized access to its branded consumer-card system. Linking identity details to wallets creates targeted-phishing risks beyond card misuse. Gnosis Pay said its enterprise white-label platform remained unaffected and made 3D Secure mandatory for online card payments. The affected consumer system was already scheduled for retirement on December 20, leaving customer migration and continued protection of the legacy system as distinct tasks for the company and its card-program partners.

news.title: Claude Adds Plaid-Connected Account Analysis, Not Payment Execution
news.body: Anthropic introduced a U.S. Personal Finance beta that connects accounts through Plaid for eligible paid subscribers, supplying balances, credit limits and up to 24 months of transactions. The service cannot move or invest money. That places the launch in financial information and analysis rather than payment initiation, with personal-finance apps and banks’ digital channels as competing interfaces. PYMNTS notes that balances may lag by one or two days, limiting how current an account picture the assistant can provide.

perspective: BILL reports faster AI-assisted underwriting as FinCEN and the Federal Reserve withdraw proposed cross-border transfer-record requirements.

curiosity.text: The U.S. Treasury introduced Series I savings bonds in 1998, but their inflation protection works through interest rates—not inflation-indexed principal. Each bond combines a fixed rate with an inflation component that Treasury recalculates every May and November. The counterintuitive safeguard: deflation can reduce the composite interest rate to zero, but never below zero. Source: U.S. Treasury, “About I Bonds” — https://www.treasurydirect.gov/savings-bonds/i-bonds/
